Playbook.name: QA - Office 365 Medium Severity - SOC Playbook

Reference.title: MITRE ATT and CK T1567 Exfiltration Over Web Service

ExecutiveSummary.Overview: This rule surfaces Medium-severity Microsoft 365 Security and Compliance alerts (o365.audit.Severity == "Medium"). At JCB these are Data Loss Prevention matches, dominated by the endpoint payment-card policies (DLP-jcb-card-Devices and its browser variant). Being a severity-based catch-all, the specific technique depends on the underlying policy; the common case is card / sensitive data touched on a device or browser. Triage question: is this a genuine attempt to move sensitive data (or an account being misused), or authorised activity / a transfer the policy already blocked? Medium is a lower-urgency signal than the High-severity variant but is triaged the same way, with an eye for a pattern that is escalating toward High.
ExecutiveSummary.BusinessImpact: For a bank, repeated Medium DLP matches on card or sensitive data — especially clustered on one user or escalating to High — can be an early indicator of data staging or insider misuse before a larger loss. Handling them well keeps small leaks from becoming reportable breaches.

Assets.AssetType: Microsoft 365 tenant (JCB) — Exchange Online, SharePoint/OneDrive, endpoint DLP; Microsoft Purview / Security and Compliance

TelemetryRequirements.Requirement: M365 unified audit via Elastic Agent — verified live at JCB (8.1M docs/30d). Medium-severity events are Security and Compliance alerts: event.code == "SecurityComplianceAlerts", event.provider == "SecurityComplianceCenter", event.action IN ("AlertTriggered","AlertEntityGenerated","AlertUpdated"), o365.audit.Severity == "Medium" (about 3,350 events/30d at JCB, dominated by endpoint card-DLP).

JCB-specific: the affected user/mailbox is in o365.audit.ObjectId as an email (case varies, e.g. jcbank.com.jo vs JCBANK.COM.JO) — match case-insensitively. rule.name is the DLP/alert policy name. o365.audit.Operation is NOT populated at JCB; the action is in event.action. These alert records carry no source.ip. O365 ingest lag is 20-60 min (compliance alerts can lag more); queries use a 4h window.

Signal.Name: QA - Office 365 Medium Severity
Signal.Details: An M365 Security and Compliance alert with o365.audit.Severity == "Medium" for an entity.

Input.name: $entity
Input.description: The affected user / mailbox email the alert is about (o365.audit.ObjectId).

InitialAssessment.Rule: Weigh the full evidence story per the ClassificationGuidance — identify the policy that matched and whether real sensitive data actually moved (and whether it was blocked), and whether this is part of an escalating pattern, not just that an alert fired.

Investigation.Goal: Determine whether the Medium-severity M365 compliance alert reflects a genuine data-loss / account-misuse event or an escalating pattern, or authorised activity / a transfer the policy already blocked.

Step.name: Identify the alert and the policy that matched
Step.Purpose: Pull the Medium-severity compliance alert(s) for this entity and read the policy name (rule.name) and the alert lifecycle actions — this tells you what sensitive data and channel triggered it.
Step.Query: FROM logs-o365.audit-* | WHERE @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours AND o365.audit.Severity == "Medium" AND TO_LOWER(o365.audit.ObjectId) == TO_LOWER("$entity") | KEEP @timestamp, o365.audit.Severity, rule.name, event.action, event.provider, o365.audit.ObjectId, o365.audit.AlertId | SORT @timestamp DESC | LIMIT 25
Step.AnalystNotes: rule.name names the DLP/compliance policy (at JCB, commonly DLP-jcb-card-Devices and its browser variant). Use the AlertId to open the full alert in the Microsoft Purview / Defender portal for the matched content and the block/allow action.

Step.name: Is this a one-off, a pattern, or escalating to High
Step.Purpose: Summarise this entity's Medium and High compliance alerts across the window — several policies, a burst, or a rise to High severity is far more concerning than a single Medium match.
Step.Query: FROM logs-o365.audit-* | WHERE @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours AND o365.audit.Severity IN ("Medium","High") AND TO_LOWER(o365.audit.ObjectId) == TO_LOWER("$entity") | STATS alerts = COUNT(*), policies = VALUES(rule.name), severities = VALUES(o365.audit.Severity), first_seen = MIN(@timestamp), last_seen = MAX(@timestamp) | LIMIT 1
Step.AnalystNotes: If severities includes "High" or multiple distinct policies appear for one entity, raise the priority — Medium matches that cluster or escalate often precede a larger loss.

Step.name: Corroborate with the entity's real data-movement activity
Step.Purpose: Look at the affected user's actual M365 action profile in the window — sends, mailbox and attachment access, downloads and external sharing — to judge whether real data movement backs the DLP alert.
Step.Query: FROM logs-o365.audit-* | WHERE @timestamp >= NOW() - 4 hours AND (TO_LOWER(user.name) == TO_LOWER("$entity") OR TO_LOWER(user.email) == TO_LOWER("$entity")) | STATS events = COUNT(*), sources = VALUES(source.ip) BY event.action | SORT events DESC | LIMIT 20
Step.AnalystNotes: The entity's full action profile in the window (JCB keys the actor as the short user.name and the email user.email; this query matches either). Exfil-relevant actions to weigh: Send / SendAs, MailItemsAccessed, AttachmentAccess, FileDownloadedFromBrowser / FileSyncDownloadedFull, FileUploaded, AnonymousLinkCreated / SharingInvitationCreated. A spike in these, or activity from an unfamiliar source (JCB egress NAT is 94.249.88.0/24; Microsoft service IPs are normal), corroborates real data movement. Little activity, or a Purview outcome showing the transfer was blocked, points to a benign/blocked event.

Node.Condition: A sensitive-data DLP policy matched real content (INV-01), INV-02 shows a cluster or escalation to High, and INV-03 shows corroborating data movement (external send/share, bulk download) that was allowed.
Node.Result: True Positive (Sensitive Data Loss — contain, scope the exposure, notify compliance)

Node.Condition: The activity is authorised business (an approved recipient/process) OR the DLP policy blocked the transfer so no data actually left (proven-blocked).
The policy is mis-scoped or over-matching (matching non-sensitive content, or a routine internal device/browser flow it should exclude), producing Medium-severity noise.
Sensitive content plausibly moved but the recipient, the intent or whether it was blocked cannot be confirmed from telemetry alone.

FalsePositive.Definition: Authorised business activity, or a transfer the DLP policy already blocked so no data left.

Indicators.Item: Recipient/process is an approved business counterpart or internal system.
The alert / Purview record shows the action was blocked (BlockAccess) — proven-blocked.
INV-02 shows a single isolated Medium match and INV-03 shows no unusual external send/share or bulk download.

SOCAction.Item: Confirm the business context or the block in Purview; document; close as false_positive.

TruePositive.Definition: Sensitive data actually moved — a genuine data-loss event, possibly staging or insider misuse, possibly via a compromised account.

Indicators.Item: Sensitive-data policy (e.g. card) matched and the transfer was allowed.
A cluster of Medium matches or escalation to High for the same entity.
Corroborating external sharing / send / bulk download around the alert time.

SOCAction.Item: Contain the account (disable/reset, revoke sessions/tokens) if misuse or compromise is indicated; preserve the Purview alert and matched content.
Scope what data moved and to whom; escalate to IR if the pattern is significant; notify compliance / data-protection as required.

Misconfiguration.Definition: The DLP/compliance policy is mis-scoped and over-matching, generating Medium-severity noise.

Indicators.Item: Matches are on non-sensitive or routine internal device/browser content.
The same benign flow trips the policy repeatedly for many users.

SOCAction.Item: Refer the policy to the Purview/DLP owners for tuning; document the over-match pattern.

Phase.name: Immediate Actions (0-30 minutes)
Phase.Action: Identify the matched policy and entity (INV-01); check for clustering or escalation to High (INV-02).
Open the alert in Purview/Defender via the AlertId to see the content and block/allow action.

Phase.name: Containment and Eradication (hours)
Phase.Action: If misuse/compromise or allowed egress is indicated, contain the account (disable/reset, revoke sessions and tokens) and remove any attacker persistence.
Scope the exposure using INV-03 and the Purview record: what data, to whom, over which channel.

Phase.name: Recovery and Hardening (days)
Phase.Action: Where a real loss occurred, complete data-loss / breach notification as required; consider tightening enforcement (block vs audit) on the matched policy; user-awareness follow-up.
Refer over-matching policies to the DLP owners for tuning to reduce Medium-severity noise.

Escalation.Trigger: A cluster of Medium matches or escalation to High for one entity, allowed egress of sensitive data, corroborated real data movement, or unconfirmed scope of exposure.

FalsePositiveClosure.Item: Authorised business activity or a proven block confirmed in Purview; documented; no data left.

TruePositiveClosure.Item: Account contained where needed; exposure scoped (data, recipient, channel); compliance notified where required; policy enforcement reviewed.
